observations.classification: Test qualification gap; not a demonstrated runtime vulnerability
observations.summary: Router invariant negative metadata handler reverts on unexpected success under fail_on_revert=false, instead of recording a persistent acceptance count checked by an invariant. The bad-metadata action alone therefore does not independently establish rejection. Separate unit and fuzz tests do assert metadata rejection.
observations.remediation: Track unexpected acceptance in a persistent counter and assert zero, or make the handler report the failure through an invariant-compatible assertion policy. Keep explicit unit/fuzz guards.
observations.validation: Static source inference, no mutation/testing executed.

observations.classification: Test qualification gap; not a demonstrated runtime vulnerability
observations.summary: EchidnaRouter.payFotToken does not record unexpected success. Its properties check fee-on-transfer token retention at the router but not recipient accounting for that token; successful lossy forwarding without router retention would not violate those properties. Separate Foundry unit/fuzz/invariant suites do assert rejection.
observations.remediation: Record any successful lossy-token call as a property failure, and keep a reachability measure for the negative case.

observations.summary: Immutable fee-recipient payment legs are an availability dependency: token freezing or a native-rejecting fee recipient can prevent fee-bearing payments. No rotation/admin escape is part of core router design. Validate the selected fee account, monitor token support, and keep a replacement deployment/manifest recovery plan.
observations.validation: Current contract source plus inspected pre-existing regression tests; not live-chain confirmation.

observations.summary: A router announcement alone authenticates neither invoice payment intent nor token identity/curve ownership; scanner verification must retain cryptographic derivation, approved contract/token and independent transfer evidence checks. Main/candidate adapters enforce additional evidence; no bypass established.

Core gas-buffer forwarding is deliberately untaxed and bounded by the payer-supplied maximum rather than a protocol cap. Fee rounding and buffer semantics are not a universal levy on native value. Relayer sponsorship also remains exposed to state changes after simulation and arbitrary token execution cost. These do not establish diversion of a valid signed sweep.
observations.remediation: Align fee claims with contract semantics; relayer services need a token allowlist, bounded simulation/gas spending and sponsor rate limits. Hosted service implementations are outside this audit.
observations.validation: Static contract and existing test review only.
